subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should this PR land with the doctor migration that removes legacy `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` and disables enabled OTLP-signal configs, or should OpenClaw keep `grpc` accepted until real gRPC export exists?
rationale: The code defect is clear, but removing a previously shipped config value is an upgrade and operator-behavior decision that automation should not settle on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept doctor-mediated rejection
options.body: Land this PR with the current migration semantics: remove legacy `grpc`, preserve stdout-only logs, and require operators to choose OTLP/HTTP before re-enabling failed OTLP signals.

options.title: Require different migration semantics
options.body: Keep the PR open for a maintainer-specified adjustment, such as preserving `enabled` differently or changing the warning/removal window before merge.

options.title: Defer until real gRPC export
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep the existing config value until the diagnostics-otel plugin implements and proves gRPC exporters.

recommendation.title: Accept doctor-mediated rejection
recommendation.body: Land this PR with the current migration semantics: remove legacy `grpc`, preserve stdout-only logs, and require operators to choose OTLP/HTTP before re-enabling failed OTLP signals.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail points to the original diagnostics exporter/config introduction, and this decision is about that product/config contract.
